title: compact-credential-lease-adapter-and-zero-copy-stream-handles
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a cross-SDK compact credential lease adapter (opt-in) and zero-copy stream handle primitives for higher-throughput streaming. Tweaks retry profiles and bumps Python/TS/Go SDK minor versions.
description:
Motivation: Several high-throughput streaming customers observed CPU pressure and extra memory churn from repeated token handoffs and per-chunk byte copies. This PR introduces two focused changes to reduce client-side cost and improve cross-SDK ergonomics: 1) a compact CredentialLease adapter that standardizes short-lived token leases and proactive refresh logic across SDKs, and 2) a zero-copy stream handle layer that exposes buffer views to avoid per-chunk allocations.

Summary of changes: - New compact credential lease adapter (sdk/shared/lease): a tiny, dependency-free lease interface and producer that SDKs can opt into. It supports lease.acquire(timeout_ms) -> LeaseHandle (id, expiry, token), proactive refresh callback registration, and a light metrics hook. The adapter is intentionally minimal so it can be embedded into hosted or private deployments without heavy runtime coupling. - Python: adds sdk/python/redwood/auth/lease.py (memoryview-based streaming token appender), integrates lease warmup in the session factory, adjusts retry backoff presets for short-lived tokens. - TypeScript: introduces src/stream/zero_copy_handle.ts that returns Uint8Array views referencing the underlying stream buffer; adds a thin Lease binding in src/auth/compactLease.ts. - Go: adds compact lease types in pkg/auth/compact_lease.go and a zero-copy io.Reader wrapper used by the stream consumer. - Tests: unit and integration tests for lease refresh behavior; streaming throughput microbenchmarks show a ~16% CPU reduction on medium payload workloads.

Compatibility and migration notes: - Default behavior is unchanged. The compact lease adapter is behind an opt-in flag (client config: auth.compact_lease: true). - Zero-copy handles are opt-in at client construction for languages where exposing raw buffer views is safe (python: stream_zero_copy=True, ts/go: same). Enabling zero-copy may affect code that assumed owned copies of chunks; we documented usage patterns and provided helpers to copy when required. - No server-side contract changes.

Testing and rollout: - CI: unit-tests, integration-tests, typechecks, linting all green after two reruns. - Internal canary: rolled out the opt-in flags to internal staging and to 3 beta customers for 2 weeks. Observed no regressions in end-to-end behavior and consistent CPU decreases. - Rollout plan: start as opt-in in the next SDK minor release; collect telemetry and then enable automatic suggestions in Optimize for eligible customers.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1329) - [x] Cross-SDK API surface minimal and documented - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Benchmark microbenchmarks included - [x] Release notes drafted - [x] Version bumps for each SDK package
commits: Introduce compact credential lease core and interface
Python: memoryview-based token appender and session factory wiring
TypeScript: zero-copy stream handle and compact lease binding
Go: compact lease types and zero-copy reader wrapper
Tests: lease refresh + streaming throughput microbenchmarks
Chore: bump sdk python/ts/go minor versions and docs
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Can you clarify lifetime semantics for a LeaseHandle if the underlying token is rotated mid-stream? How should consumers detect invalidation?

Author (Maya Chen): LeaseHandle includes an expiry timestamp and lease.id; adapters will emit a 'lease_invalidation' metric and the handle.owner should check expiry before sending chunk. Added note in docs and added unit test that simulates mid-stream rotation.
Priya Nair: Zero-copy on TS looks great but I worry about user code that mutates the view. Can we add a helper to get an owned copy?
Author (Maya Chen): Added toZeroCopyCopy(bufferView) helper and documented common pitfall. Also added a terse comment in zero_copy_handle.ts.
Ethan Liu: CI flaked on streaming e2e the first run; was the failure related to environment noise?
Author (Maya Chen): Flake was due to a test that assumed non-deterministic chunk boundaries; updated test to be tolerant and retriggered CI. All checks green on rerun.
